QUESTION: Mary Anne Evans was the real name of which famous novelist?
STUDENT ANSWER: Your guess is correct, Mary Anne Evans was a famous novelist who went by the pen name George Eliot. The pen name was chosen to avoid the bias that might have been associated with a female author during that time period. George Eliot wrote many well-known novels such as "Silas Marner" and "Middlemarch".

The use of a pen name is a common practice in literature, sometimes adopted to protect an author's identity or to overcome perceived biases. In this case, it allowed Evans to have her work judged on its merits alone.
